class.name: Druid
class.text: Leather, three forms and a mana bar that does not work in two of them. Wrath, Healing Touch and Mark of the Wild are yours from the start, Moonfire and Rejuvenation come at 4, Thorns at 6 and Entangling Roots at 8. At 10 you get Bear Form, Maul and your first talent point, and Cat Form follows at 20. Every line below says which form to be in before it says what to press.

card.caresAbout: the form you are in, the bar that form runs on (mana, Rage or Energy), what is bleeding and whether you can afford another shift
card.vocabulary: form, shift, Rage, Energy, combo points, bleed, root, heal over time, mana
card.soundsLike: patient and practical, a trainer who asks which form you are in before asking what you will press. A druid line names the form first
card.neverSays: the wild, the dream, any god or grove, nature as a faith (spells carry those words and the line uses them as names only)
card.test: could it be followed by someone who forgot which form they were in?

advice.say: Feral as a cat is the damage build this page advises, because you fight as a bear until Cat Form at 20 with the same points, so one set of picks covers the whole climb. The price: a cat cannot cast or heal in form. Balance casts from range and levels slowly alone.

Feral as a bear is the tank. Bear Form comes at 10, Lacerate at 25 and Primal Bite at 40 for threat. The price: it is the cat's tree, so the points that tank and the points that kill are not the same, and a respec between them costs gold.

Restoration is the healer. It kills slowly by itself, so the common road is to level as Feral and respec for dungeons. The price of that road: a respec costs gold. The price of levelling in Restoration instead: speed.

overview.who: You are three classes in one and you choose which at the pull. With no form on you cast, in Bear Form you tank, in Cat Form you stab. A form costs mana to enter and then runs on Rage or Energy.
overview.good: Doing the job in front of you. A Druid levels well as a bear or a cat, heals a group between pulls and brings a dead player back with Rebirth.
overview.bad: Staying in one place. Every shift costs mana, you cannot cast or heal in a form, and the caster specs are slow alone.
overview.resource: Mana to shift and to cast, Rage in Bear Form, and Energy and combo points in Cat Form. Entering a form takes a large part of your mana, so drink before you shift back.
overview.levelling: Bear Form from 10 and Cat Form from 20. Until 20 you fight as a bear with Maul and Swipe. After that a cat takes single monsters and a bear takes packs, with a heal and a drink between fights. Check your form before each pull.
overview.ten: You get your first talent point and Bear Form. Pick the spec: Feral is the common road for levelling and is a cat or a bear, Balance casts from range and Restoration heals. A respec costs gold.

damage.reason: You are a bear until Cat Form at 20 with the same points, so one build covers the climb. Balance casts from range and kills more slowly alone.

tank.reason: The only tanking build. Bear Form comes at 10, Lacerate at 25 and Primal Bite at 40 for threat.

heal.reason: The only healing build. It kills slowly alone, so the common road is to level as Feral and respec for dungeons.

builds.name: Feral Combat
builds.intro: Feral as a cat kills one monster at a time with Energy and combo points: Rake and Rip bleed, Claw and Shred build, Ferocious Bite finishes. Cat Form comes at 20, so levels 10 to 19 are spent in Bear Form with the same points. Levelling in Feral is the common choice on Forever, because one set of points serves the bear and the cat.
builds.line: Cat Form from 20, bleeds and a finisher. A bear until then, with the same points all the way.
builds.pathNote: (31 points in Feral Combat, 7 in Balance for Genesis and Nature's Majesty, 13 in Restoration for Heart of the Wild, Naturalist and Natural Shapeshifter.)
builds.split: the points after 40 and Shifting Power. A common end is a Balance tail, which this build follows, with Natural Shapeshifter in place of Nature's Reach, which helps spells only. Shifting Power turns mana into Energy and costs a point the tail would use. Nobody has played past 30.
builds.dry: Shred wants you behind the monster. Claw does not mind where you stand.

path.why: Maul, Swipe, Claw and Rake cost less Rage or Energy. You are a bear until 20, so it helps from the first fight, and that is why it goes first.
Swipe hits harder, and monsters notice you less while you Prowl. Swipe is your attack against a pack, and you are a bear until 20.
More movement speed in Cat Form and a better chance to dodge. Taking it now means it is full when Cat Form comes at 20.
You crit more often in Cat Form and Bear Form, so every attack you make gains from it.
In Cat Form it leaps you behind the monster, so Shred works after it. In Bear Form it holds the monster and cuts off a spell.
Claw, Rake, Shred, Maul and Swipe hit harder. These are the attacks you use all fight.
More attack power in Cat Form and Bear Form, scaled to your level. It is also the gate to Rend and Tear.
It changes how Ferocious Bite spends spare Energy, and it is the gate to Shifting Power at 40.
Shred costs less Energy. Shred is your hardest hit while you are behind the monster, so it earns each rank when you can get there.
Your party crits more often while you are in Cat Form. It is the common pick at 30, and the points it costs could go to your own damage.
Your melee crits hurt more. It follows Leader of the Pack here because both lean on crits.
Shred costs less Energy again, so you land it more often. It suits an opening from behind, which is the common one.
Your melee attacks do more to a bleeding monster. Rake and Rip keep one bleeding, so most of your fight is spent in this bonus.
Turns mana into Energy on a cooldown, for when Energy runs low. It is optional: it costs mana, and a build that skips it keeps the point for something else.
Bleeds and heals over time do a little more with each rank. Rake and Rip are both over time. This is where the tail after the main points begins.
A little more crit chance with spells and melee attacks. The build stops at two ranks and does not pair it with Nature's Reach, which only helps spells.
More Intellect, more Stamina in Bear Form and more Strength in Cat Form. It is the gate to Naturalist.
All the damage you deal rises with each rank. It comes last, after Heart of the Wild.
Shifting costs less mana, Shifting Power included. A cat that turns bear for a pack shifts a lot.

builds.name: Feral Combat
builds.intro: Feral as a bear holds monsters while a group kills them. Bear Form comes at 10. Lacerate at 25 and Primal Bite at 40 make the threat, and Frenzied Regeneration and Barkskin keep you alive. It is the cat's tree with different points.
builds.line: Bear Form from 10, Lacerate and Primal Bite for threat. It holds a pack for the group.
builds.pathNote: (43 points in Feral Combat, 8 in Restoration for Heart of the Wild and Natural Shapeshifter.)
builds.split: Rend and Tear against Natural Reaction, and Lacerate. Rend and Tear suits a dungeon tank. Natural Reaction is the other pick, and Lacerate costs points that a tank who does not run dungeons can spend elsewhere. The points after 30 are ours from the row gates, and nobody has played past 30.
builds.dry: A monster that is hitting you is not hitting anyone else, and that is the whole job.

path.why: Maul, Swipe and Primal Bite cost less Rage, so you spend it on more attacks. Rage is the only thing a bear runs on.
Swipe hits harder. Swipe is your attack against two or three monsters, and most of your threat until Lacerate.
Bash stuns longer and comes back sooner. A stun that is ready more often is a monster that does nothing more often.
Maul and Swipe hit harder. It is also the gate to Lacerate at 25, so these two points have to come first.
In Bear Form it holds a monster and cuts off a spell. It gets you to the monster that is running at your healer.
You crit more often in Cat Form and Bear Form. It is also the gate to Blood Frenzy.
A bleed that stacks 5 times and makes a lot of threat. You tank dungeons, so you take it. A bear that only quests can spend the point elsewhere.
More attack power in Bear Form, scaled to your level, so your swings make more threat. It is the gate to Rend and Tear.
A critical strike gives you extra Rage. More Rage is more Maul and Swipe, so a crit helps your threat twice.
Your party crits more often while you are in Bear Form. The group gets it for free, and Primal Bite at 40 needs it.
A critical strike gives you extra Rage. More Rage is more Maul and Swipe, so a crit helps your threat twice.
More armour in Bear Form. Armour stops part of every hit, and a tank takes the most hits. It is the usual pick for a dungeon tank.
Your melee attacks do more to a bleeding monster. Lacerate keeps one bleeding, so Maul and Swipe gain from it on every pull.
A heavy bite that makes a lot of threat, on a short cooldown. It is the pick for tanking a pack, and a bear that only quests can do without it.
You dodge more, and a dodge can give you Rage. A tank that is hit less needs less healing, and the Rage pays for Maul.
Shifting into Bear Form can give you Rage at once, so you open a pull with Rage to spend.
Your melee crits hurt more. Lacerate and Maul crit more with Sharpened Claws, so it adds threat.
More Stamina in Bear Form, which is more health to be hit with, and more Intellect for the heals between pulls.
Shifting costs less mana. You shift to heal between pulls and shift back, and each shift costs a large part of your mana.

builds.name: Balance
builds.intro: Balance casts Wrath and Starfire from range, keeps Moonfire and Insect Swarm on the monster, and shifts into Moonkin Form at 40. Eclipse makes Wrath speed up the Starfires after it. It is slow before Hurricane at 40 and every kill costs mana, so the common road is to level as Feral and come here later.
builds.line: Wrath, Starfire, Moonfire and Insect Swarm from range. Slow alone, with Moonkin Form at 40.
builds.pathNote: (41 points in Balance, 10 in Restoration for Heart of the Wild, Reflection and Naturalist.)
builds.split: whether to level it at all. Balance is playable beyond 30 and its power comes late, so the common road is to level as Feral and come here later. The cost of levelling here is speed. The first 11 points follow a level 20 order, and the rest are ours from the row gates and the priorities named for the tree. Nobody has written a full order.
builds.dry: A caster that is meleeing has already run out of mana.

path.why: Wrath casts faster and costs less mana. It is the spell you cast most until 20, so it goes first.
Your damage spells cost less mana. Every kill costs mana, and this is the cheapest way to make it last.
Your Balance spells reach further and miss less. A longer reach means you cast for longer before the monster arrives.
Moonfire hits harder and crits more. You put it on every monster, and it is the gate to Vengeance.
A little more crit chance with spells and melee attacks. It is the gate to Nature's Splendor.
Moonfire lasts longer, and so do Rejuvenation, Regrowth and Insect Swarm. A longer Moonfire is damage you pay for once.
A second damage over time that also lowers the monster's chance to hit you. It comes at 25 here, and the cost is the point it takes from the casts.
Your damage over time does more with each rank. Moonfire and Insect Swarm are both over time, so it takes all five.
Wrath makes your next Starfires cast faster. Cast Wrath, then Starfire, and the pair is quicker than either alone.
The fifth rank of Genesis, now that Eclipse is taken.
A spell crit makes your next casts faster for a short time. It is one of the Balance talents that rewards crits.
Arcane and Nature spells hit harder. Wrath, Starfire and Moonfire all count.
Raises your armour and your party's crit chance, but you cannot heal in it. It is the tree's milestone at 40.
Starfire casts faster and can stun the monster. Eclipse speeds it up again, so this is the second half of that pair.
More Intellect, which is more mana and more crit. It is the gate to Reflection and Naturalist, which suit casters.
Part of your mana regeneration keeps going while you cast. A caster runs out of mana before monsters, and this is the fix.
Your Arcane and Nature spells crit for more. Crits are where Starfire's damage is.
All the damage you deal rises with each rank, and Healing Touch casts faster. Two ranks are what the last points allow.

builds.name: Restoration
builds.intro: Restoration keeps a group alive with heals over time: Rejuvenation and Regrowth on the tank, Swiftmend when it drops, Wild Growth at 40. It kills slowly alone, so this page is for dungeons and says what to do in between. You cannot heal in a form, so you step out of one to do it.
builds.line: Rejuvenation, Regrowth and Swiftmend on a group. It kills slowly alone, so it is for dungeons.
builds.pathNote: (51 points in Restoration, every talent of the tree.)
builds.split: whether to level in it at all. The common road is to level as Feral and respec for dungeons, which costs gold. Levelling in Restoration instead costs speed, because it kills slowly alone. The first 13 points are a healer's opening, and the order after that is ours from the row gates. Nobody has played past 30.
builds.dry: A heal that lands after the tank has died heals no one.

path.why: A hit is less likely to delay your cast. A healer is hit while healing, so it goes first.
Healing Touch casts faster, and all your damage rises. It is the gate to Nature's Swiftness at 30, so it goes second.
Part of your mana regeneration keeps going while you cast. A healer casts all the time, so this pays back every fight.
Every healing spell you cast heals a little more with each rank.
Heals at once a target that has your Rejuvenation or Regrowth on it. It is your emergency button, and it comes at 25.
Rejuvenation heals more, and it is the gate to Improved Regrowth. Rejuvenation is the heal you keep on the tank.
Every healing spell you cast heals a little more with each rank.
Your next Nature spell is instant. Use it on Healing Touch when the tank is about to die.
More Spirit, so more mana regeneration. It is the gate to Wild Growth at 40.
Every healing spell you cast heals a little more with each rank.
Regrowth crits more often. Regrowth is the heal for a tank who is falling behind.
A heal over time on a target and its party, with a long cast. It costs a lot of mana, so save it for emergencies.
More Intellect, which is more mana, and more Stamina in Bear Form for the times you shift.
Healing Touch and Tranquility cost less mana. You cast Healing Touch a lot, and mana is what ends a dungeon.
When Rejuvenation or Regrowth runs out, the target is healed for as much as your Spirit. Nobody has played it yet, so this is what the talent says.
Every healing spell you cast heals a little more with each rank.
Tranquility makes no threat and comes back sooner. It is a party heal you can use more than once in a hard fight.
Your Nature and Arcane spells make less threat. A heal that pulls the monster onto you is a heal that goes wrong.
Shifting costs less mana. You shift to travel or to fight alone, then back to heal.
